title: Sherpa Tensing — Camp Four: Present Perfect Simple (B1)
description: Camp three was the ground you crossed and left. Camp four is the ground still roped to you. The present perfect describes a past that has not been cut…

hero.lede: Camp three was the ground you crossed and left. Camp four is the ground still roped to you. The present perfect describes a past that has not been cut loose — a period still running, an experience with no date on it, or something that happened moments ago and is still showing.

cards.head: An unfinished time period
cards.body: The period started in the past and is still running now.
cards.ex: "I have lived here for ten years." — and I still do

cards.head: An unspecified time
cards.body: It happened, but when is not stated and does not matter.

cards.head: A very recent action
cards.body: Finished moments ago, with the result still in front of you.
cards.ex: "Doris has just made coffee." — it is still hot

cards.head: Life experience, so far
cards.body: A running total, counted up to the present moment.
cards.ex: "I have been there a few times."

cards.head: A change up to now
cards.body: The situation is different from how it was.
cards.ex: "The village has grown since the road opened."

cards.head: Something still outstanding
cards.body: Expected, not done yet — and the door is still open.

charts.head: The line that decides it
charts.note: Give the sentence a finished, stated time and it falls back to camp three. This is the single test that settles almost every case.

head: Time is…
Tense
Example
rows: I have lived here for ten years.

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: subject + have not (haven't) / has not (hasn't) + past participle

cards.head: Wh- questions
cards.body: question word + have / has + subject + past participle?

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Only the auxiliary changes — has for he, she and it, have for everyone else. The participle never moves. Using the verb "to work" as the model.

charts.head: Irregular past participles worth carrying
charts.note: The participle is the third form, and it is not always the past simple. Getting went and been the wrong way round is the most common slip at this camp.

charts.head: The words that send you back to camp three
charts.note: These name a finished time, so they take the past simple — never the present perfect.

signals.head: Time still running
items: for — for ten years, for a while

diagram.intro: The past simple block on the left is closed — a stated time, over. Everything turquoise is still attached to the present: a period that has not ended, an experience with no date on it, and something that finished moments ago and is still showing. Click any block — or any bar below it — to name it and see it in sentences.

bars.head: Past simple — finished, specified time
bars.body: The moment is stated or clearly understood, and it is over. Nothing reaches forward from it.

bars.head: Unfinished time — the period is still running
bars.body: It started in the past and has not ended. For and since live here.
examples: I have lived here for ten years.
She has worked at the clinic since April.

bars.head: Unspecified time — when is not the point
bars.body: It happened at some point in a life, and no date is given. Ask for one and you drop back to past simple.
examples: Yes — I have been there a few times.

bars.head: Very recent — the result is still here
bars.body: Finished moments ago, and you can still see it. Just, already and yet live here.

bars.head: Now — present simple
bars.body: The moment you are speaking from. Everything turquoise above is still attached to this column.

quiz.prompt: I _____ here for ten years — and I'm still here. (live)
quiz.hint: The ten years are not over.
quiz.explain: The period is still running, so the present perfect keeps it attached to now: have lived.

quiz.hint: "Ten years ago" is a finished, stated time.
quiz.explain: A stated finished time sends you back to camp three: past simple, moved.

quiz.hint: No time is given — the question is about experience.
quiz.explain: With ever and no stated time, the present perfect asks about experience: Have you ever been…?

quiz.prompt: Doris has just _____ coffee — it's still hot. (make)
quiz.hint: Have / has takes the past participle, not the past simple.
quiz.explain: Has + past participle. Make → made → made, so: has just made.

quiz.prompt: She _____ at the clinic since April. (work)
quiz.hint: Since points at a starting point that runs up to now.
quiz.explain: Since anchors an unfinished period, so the present perfect: has worked.

quiz.hint: Yet belongs to something still outstanding.
quiz.explain: Yet marks something expected but not done, which keeps it in the present perfect: Have they finished… yet?

quiz.hint: Last spring names a finished time.
quiz.explain: Last spring is stated and finished — past simple, went. Have gone would clash with it.

quiz.hint: A life experience, counted up to now.
quiz.explain: Never with no stated time is experience up to the present: has never eaten.

quiz.hint: How long asks about a period still running.
quiz.explain: How long + present perfect measures a period that reaches the present: How long have you known her?

quiz.prompt: The village _____ a lot since the road opened. (change)
quiz.hint: Since again — and the change is visible now.
quiz.explain: Since opens a period that runs to now, and the result is in front of you: has changed.

results: Camp struck. Every step behind you accounted for.
Solid progress. A couple of loose stones to check before camp four.
Good first attempt. Worth another pass before moving on.
